statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail sits at the low end of the watch band while Stress remains high on a two-decade-high yield backdrop.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped state stays WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 13:30 to 15:00 UTC, covering the US cash open and the stacked 14:00 UTC JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence releases. Outside that window the published forecast returns to the low and watch bands.
headline: Two-way overnight NQ recovery keeps Tail contained while two-decade-high yields hold Stress elevated
body: NQ front-month traded a 30,373-30,616 overnight range and sits near 30,565, effectively unchanged on the session after fully retracing its Asian-hours dip. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Monday at 30,276.81, down 1.08%, but finished roughly 200 points above its 30,081.06 session low, and the index has held a rough 30,081-30,708 band across four sessions. Those retracements are the reason Tail stays in the low watch band despite a genuinely difficult macro backdrop. That backdrop is severe: the 10-year Treasury yield reached about 5.24% on Monday after touching 5.272%, a fresh two-decade high, with the 30-year at 5.56%, and markets now price roughly a 70% probability of a Federal Reserve rate increase in October. WTI crude is near $93.50, up about 1%, with the Strait of Hormuz still closed after the US rejected Iran's conditional seven-day reopening proposal. Semiconductors led Monday's decline, with ARM down 8.7%, QCOM down 7.2% and INTC down 5.7%, while NVDA rose 1.7% on a large buyback and AI-safety announcement. Cboe notes the divergence directly: rates volatility spiked toward a one-year high while the VIX hovered near a one-year low around 14.9 and equity volatility ended the week unchanged. Under the risk contract that combination is a Stress and Confidence story rather than a Tail story, because no persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or repeated extension after failed retracement has been observed. The main residual mechanism to monitor is a delayed second leg transmitted through the long end of the curve.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 published hours stayed inside the low and watch bands apart from two single-hour steps into the elevated band at 09:00 and 14:00 UTC on Monday, both of which reverted within an hour. Tail troughed at 17 through the Monday evening and early Tuesday overnight session and has oscillated between 20 and 24 since 01:00 UTC as the European handover approached. Stress never fell below 76 across the window, reflecting a persistent high-yield and high-oil backdrop rather than any single event. Confidence held between 83 and 88 throughout.
outlookSummary: The published forecast keeps Tail in the low and watch bands for most of the next 24 hours, with a single elevated-band hour at 14:00 UTC where JOLTS Job Openings, JOLTS Job Quits and CB Consumer Confidence all print 30 minutes into the US cash session. That stacking of the opening auction with a high-impact release is the narrow flagged window, and Tail is modelled to decay back into the watch band by 15:00 UTC on an orderly price-discovery assumption. Overnight hours into Wednesday return to the low band before Stress edges up again ahead of the ADP, core PCE and final Q2 GDP block at 12:15 and 12:30 UTC Wednesday. Every forecast hour beyond the current one describes conditional risk, not observed structure.
